subject.title: [Feature]: `openclaw backup`: support manifest-backed intentional omissions for protected or reconstructable runtime paths

question: Which permanent omission contract should `openclaw backup` support without weakening its fail-closed completeness guarantee?
rationale: The code can implement several safe-looking shapes, but maintainers must define who owns omission policy, whether persistent configuration is justified, what offline verification promises, and whether broad rules are ever acceptable.

options.title: Versioned exact-path plan
options.body: Add an explicit plan input with traversal-safe exact paths, required classifications and recovery guidance, resolved creation-time observations, and no wildcard support initially.

options.title: Built-in datasets only
options.body: Allow omissions only for narrowly defined OpenClaw-owned reconstructable datasets, avoiding an operator-configurable general exclusion surface.

options.title: Retain strict failure
options.body: Decline omission support and preserve the current requirement that operators relocate data, adjust the selected backup scope, or use an external producer.

recommendation.title: Versioned exact-path plan
recommendation.body: Add an explicit plan input with traversal-safe exact paths, required classifications and recovery guidance, resolved creation-time observations, and no wildcard support initially.

likelyOwner.reason: The original history shows the strongest ownership of backup planning, validation, and fail-closed hardening.
